excerpt: Shift Technology is a Paris-based company selling AI agents for insurance claims, fraud, subrogation and payment integrity. Funding, customers and alternatives.
content:
Shift Technology sells AI software to insurance companies. It began with insurance fraud detection: scanning claims and flagging suspicious patterns for investigators. It has since widened into claims automation and now describes its product as agents that transform insurers' most critical work. Its current solutions cover coverage and liability decisions, fraud and risk, subrogation (recovering money from other insurers), injury claims, and payment integrity for health insurers.

Shift was founded in Paris; TechCrunch reported it was founded in 2014, and Built In named the founders as David Durrleman, Eric Sibony and Jeremy Jawish. In May 2021 it raised a $220 million Series D led by Advent International through Advent Tech, with Avenir and existing investors Accel, Bessemer Venture Partners, General Catalyst and Iris Capital. TechCrunch reported that the round valued Shift at more than $1 billion and brought total funding to about $320 million. At the time the company said it served more than 100 customers in 25 countries and had analysed close to 2 billion claims.

Shift's website now claims that all of the top five US property and casualty insurers use it, that it has analysed more than 4 billion policies, claims and documents, and that it has more than 120 customers in over 30 countries. Customers shown there include AXA, Amica, Assurant and Elephant. These are the company's own figures.

Shift does not publish prices. It sells enterprise contracts to insurers, so it is relevant to claims, fraud and special investigation teams at insurance carriers, not to individuals or small agencies.

This profile is put together from the company's own pages and published reporting, checked on 15 October 2026. We have not tested the product, and nothing here is paid placement.
